label: sea

protocol.scope: Every one of 2,274 source images, viewed on all 48 numbered contact sheets with corresponding luminance histograms.
protocol.include: Recognizable ordinary daylight sea/ocean with substantial clearly blue/cyan water, reasonably water-dominant (roughly at least one third of the image), natural palette. White surf/clouds and small distant boats or people are acceptable when blue/cyan sea remains substantial and recognizable.
protocol.exclude: Gray/green/brown/nonblue water; sunset, twilight, night or monochrome; sand, sky, city or objects dominating instead of water; close-up people, boats, animals or shells; underwater subjects; nonphotos; obvious watermarks, text or artificial frames; ambiguously mixed scenes.
protocol.uncertaintyPolicy: Conservative exclusion when palette, recognizable sea subject or water coverage was ambiguous at the source resolution. Domain restrictions do not imply incorrect original class labels.
protocol.histogramUse: The luminance histogram displayed beside each thumbnail was visually available. No model inference, accuracy, prediction, frozen gate distance or automatic palette threshold was used to make manual decisions. Bright foam and dark blue daylight water may remain and overlap other classes in luminance.
protocol.sourcePolicy: Originals unchanged. Duplicate/provenance analysis and grouped splitting are separate from manual review.

recheckNotes: Direct original-image review confirmed selected blue/cyan examples and identified two conservative refinements: 1557 excluded for predominantly silver/glare water; 1808 excluded because white spray leaves insufficient clearly blue/cyan water. All these originals are 150 by 150 pixels.
